recommendation: Keep the no-change audit and do not restore FHIR-37590's R5 hyphen-prefix sentence. The current text is correct after the later FHIR-53569 decision, and the related issue is already represented on the combined branch.
issue_request: FHIR-37590 was Published/Not Persuasive with Modification for R5. It challenged guidance recommending search parameters that start with '-' and observed that SearchParameter.name does not allow hyphens; the approved resolution clarified that the URL label is SearchParameter.code, not SearchParameter.name, and changed the guidance to recommend custom SearchParameter codes starting with a hyphen.
initial_application: Git commit 94e30939143f7cb4c22d5b624063f182b61d152e applied FHIR-37590 by changing source/search.html to say servers SHOULD define custom search parameters with codes starting with a hyphen. The SearchParameter.name constraint was intentionally left unchanged because Jira distinguished it from SearchParameter.code.
additional_context: FHIR-53569 later revisited the same hyphen-prefix guidance after implementers identified a real ambiguity with _sort and leading hyphens. It was Applied/Persuasive with Modification for R6, and source commit 8b4082caae2d890a9164d9119c7db8722a31f172 replaced the hyphen recommendation with organization-scoped alphanumeric prefix guidance. The combined branch already contains Issue-Reconcile-Key FHIR-53569 at 5a5c6a7140293d25b3ad74c28e7f248f20094d02, which completed the later decision by adding the approved CapabilityStatement naming guidance paragraph.
reconciliation: No source files were changed for FHIR-37590. Current source/search.html contains the later alphanumeric-prefix guidance and CapabilityStatement client SHALL, while source/searchparameter/structuredefinition-SearchParameter.xml still preserves the SearchParameter.name versus SearchParameter.code distinction that mattered to FHIR-37590.
